We reunited at the ruined city of Troy, where the legions of fallen warriors' ghosts seemed to claw at the souls of the living. As comrades we had completed our epic journey together, but the final descent into the Trojan underground he faced alone.

We had travelled and fought as companions to reach the ruined city of Troy. We had waited for the Spartan's return for long enough.Electra ordered the remaining troops into the ruins, and the three of us made the descent into the darkness to find our friend.
We had lost our city, but the war was not over. As we made our way out of the Trojan underground, the city held one more challenge.

None of us could truly believe that our great Spartan city had been decimated by the Romans. Our epic quest to save our homeland would be replaced by our desire to prevent the Empire's brutal expansion. The Spartan was even more determined to stop Tiberius, and so headed North towards Rome while we returned to Sparta to salvage what we could. We agreed to meet in the occupied city of Athens. To the freedom-loving Athenians, the occupation was almost too much to bear. The Romans crushed any signs of dissent with brutal efficiency. But one man was not afraid - the scientist and philosopher Archimedes.

Archimedes was indebted to the Spartan. The news that the Spartan had single-handedly protected Archimedes from the assassin's blades quickly spread throughout the city. The oppressed Athenians suddenly had a glimmer of hope. Pollux and I had witnessed the devastation of Sparta first-hand; all we could do now was to rejoin the Spartan and fight shoulder to shoulder with him once again.
The future of Athens lay within the walls of Sejanus' mansion. Archimedes invention, the Eye of Apollo, held the key to the city's freedom. All we had to do, was to reach it.

The only way we could reach Rome to end Tiberius' reign of terror meant crossing the treacherous Alps, in the heart of Roman territory. There was only one pass through the Alps which was guarded by a massive fortress; the Gates of Saturn. I entrusted Electra to stay in Athens to ensure my brother's remains were afforded the respect they deserved. Meanwhile, the Spartan and I had to find a way through the Roman barricades.

The attack on the Gates of Saturn was over - we had made it across the Alps and Rome was finally within our sights. A direct attack was out of the question - the city was the most heavily fortified in the Empire. The plan was that Electra and I would sneak into Rome to destroy as much of the city as possible. The Spartan, meanwhile, would attempt to get to the heart of Empire and Emperor Tiberius via the underground aqueducts. We'd all heard the rumours about the inhabitants of Rome's underworld...

While the Spartan made his way through the catacombs beneath the city, Electra and I took the sappers a different way. By luck - or the favor of the gods - we found a way into the Colosseum, and planted the explosives. We had learned that the Emperor would be watching the games later that day. If we were lucky, we'd blow him to Hades. If not, we'd create an effective diversion for the Spartan.
